subject.title: fix(agents): skip preemptive overflow check when context engine owns compaction

question: Should ownsCompaction sessions rely on provider overflow recovery when the context engine falls back, or must the local aggregate guard remain active in that fallback path?
rationale: The patch fixes a real false-positive path, but it also changes the upgraded failure boundary for engine exceptions from local pre-submission guard to provider rejection.

options.title: Gate skip on engine success
options.body: Track successful engine assembly for the current transform and keep the aggregate guard active when the hook falls back to raw provider messages.

options.title: Accept provider fallback
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally rely on provider context-overflow recovery after engine-loop failure, accepting the compatibility and availability tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Gate skip on engine success
recommendation.body: Track successful engine assembly for the current transform and keep the aggregate guard active when the hook falls back to raw provider messages.

likelyOwner.reason: They are already in the PR discussion and recently owned adjacent context-engine overflow recovery and precheck decisions.
